A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core problems, and principal hardness results. All 16 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, figures, and references. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical reductions and proofs, without original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 adds an algorithm and theoretical convergence analysis, but reports no original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: New Section 4.2 introduces projected gradient descent on the existing dual minimization formulation, followed by multiplier recovery and normalization to construct approximate Nash equilibria. This adds a substantive algorithm beyond v1's reductions and exact-KKT equilibrium construction.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. Additional references to Dota and graph transduction in v2 provide motivation, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods. The new comparison with Anagnostides et al. [AKP+23] concerns theoretical runtime guarantees, not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols. The new payoff bounds and PGD specifications concern theoretical assumptions and the proposed algorithm, not evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, error analyses, or empirical case studies. Section 4.2 adds mathematical analysis.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, statistical uncertainty estimates, and significance tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured results or experimental findings. Changes to approximation bounds and asymptotic running time are theoretical results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the copy-gadget parameter from 2ε²/Z to ε/T, restores the missing T factor in the derivative, and revises Claim 3.1 from ε²/Z accuracy with ε≤1/13 to ε/10 accuracy with ε≤1. New Section 4.2 adds approximate-KKT and normal-cone definitions, equilibrium-conversion arguments, and Theorem 4.2 claiming O(poly(|Γ|)/ε²) runtime for payoffs in [-1,1].

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 add a constructive algorithm with 1/ε² runtime dependence as a main contribution. v2 claims a quadratic improvement in ε-dependence over AKP+23 while acknowledging that their setting is more general. The original CLS-hardness and completeness claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the claimed algorithmic improvement to polymatrix structure and qualifies its comparison with more general adversarial games. Section 5 now frames the optimal approximation-rate question around the claimed 1/ε² bound, replacing v1's generic discussion of polynomial dependence.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies the PGD stepsize 1/L, gradient-mapping stopping threshold ε/2, required KKT accuracy, and a convex program for recovering multipliers. These provide technical prescriptions absent from v1; neither version supplies implementation code or computational resource information.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 expands positioning through coordination games on graphs, graph transduction, and linearly convergent minmax algorithms. v2 also attributes resolution of previously open single-adversary and uncoupled-minmax questions to APSY25 and BC26, respectively, and introduces a runtime comparison with AKP+23.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain. v2 expands the abstract and related-work discussion, divides Section 4 into membership and algorithm subsections, updates open problems and affiliations, and makes localized wording corrections.

P2.justification: The two figures and their captions are retained without substantive redesign. Figure 2 now precedes Section 2.2 rather than interrupting Definition 4, and text and mathematical displays are reflowed. No tables or additional figures appear.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs the reduction's derivative scaling and strengthens its approximation guarantee, while updating context and adding a potentially valuable algorithm. However, Section 4.2 projects x separately and then resets γ, although equation (7) couples these variables. This procedure need not be the Euclidean projection whose optimality the convergence proof invokes. The proof improvements therefore coexist with an unresolved correctness issue in the new headline algorithm, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
